titleBlock.headline: GlyNAC Randomized Clinical Trial: Restoring Intracellular Glutathione Reverses Oxidative Stress, Mitochondrial Dysfunction & Physical Decline in Older Adults
titleBlock.authors: Kumar, P., Liu, C., Suliburk, J., Hsu, J.W., Muthupillai, R., Jahoor, F., Minard, C.G., Taffet, G.E. & Sekhar, R.V.
titleBlock.journal: The Journals of Gerontology: Series A
titleBlock.summary: In a 16-week double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial at Baylor College of Medicine (NCT01870193) comparing older adults (aged 61–80 years, n = 24 randomized to GlyNAC vs. isonitrogenous alanine placebo) against young adult controls (aged 21–40 years, n = 12), oral GlyNAC (100 mg/kg/day each of glycine and N-acetylcysteine) corrected intracellular RBC and muscle glutathione deficiency (+164%), lowered lipid peroxidation (TBARS) by -72%, reduced insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) by -64%, restored mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and mitophagy (PINK1), and normalized gait speed to young-adult levels.

studyOverview.title: The Question
studyOverview.content: Glutathione (GSH, γ-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinylglycine) is the most abundant endogenous intracellular antioxidant, but older adults develop severe intracellular GSH deficiency due to diminished availability of its two limiting amino acid precursors: glycine and cysteine. Can supplementing Glycine + N-Acetylcysteine (GlyNAC) in a randomized placebo-controlled trial restore tissue GSH, rescue mitochondrial bioenergetics, and improve physical function in older humans?

studyOverview.title: What They Did
studyOverview.content: Enrolled n = 24 community-dwelling older adults (ages 61–80 yr) and n = 12 young adults (ages 21–40 yr). Older adults were randomized 1:1 in a double-blind design for 16 weeks to receive either oral GlyNAC (100 mg/kg/day glycine + 100 mg/kg/day N-acetylcysteine) or an isonitrogenous alanine placebo (200 mg/kg/day), with serial measurements at 0, 2, and 16 weeks of RBC/muscle GSH, stable-isotope GSH synthesis rates, TBARS/F2-isoprostanes, calorimetry, muscle biopsy Western blots (PGC-1α, PINK1, p16, γH2AX), cytokines, HOMA-IR, and physical performance.

studyOverview.title: What They Found
studyOverview.content: While the alanine placebo group showed zero improvement across any metric, 16 weeks of GlyNAC increased RBC total GSH by +164% (p < 0.0001), cut oxidative stress (TBARS -72%, F2-isoprostanes -72%), rescued mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation (+78%) and lowered abnormal glucose oxidation, reduced IL-6 (-78%), TNF-α (-54%), and hs-CRP (-65%), cut HOMA-IR by -64%, lowered muscle p16INK4a senescence and γH2AX DNA damage, and increased gait speed (+18%, matching young adults), 6-minute walk distance, and grip strength.

biomarkerDomains.summary: At baseline, older adults had 66% lower intracellular RBC GSH and 494% higher plasma TBARS lipid peroxidation than young adults. GlyNAC restored de novo GSH synthesis enzymes (GCLC, GCLM, GSS) and normalized redox balance by Week 16.

Aged mitochondria suffer from impaired fatty-acid entry and oxidation, forcing reliance on inefficient glucose oxidation. Muscle biopsies showed GlyNAC restored PGC-1α, CPT1b, Complex I–V subunits, and PINK1-mediated mitophagy.

metrics.label: Muscle PGC-1α & PINK1 Mitophagy Protein Expression

biomarkerDomains.summary: By quenching intracellular reactive oxygen species and restoring mitochondrial beta-oxidation, GlyNAC profoundly suppressed systemic pro-inflammatory cytokines, improved endothelial function (sICAM-1/sVCAM-1), and upregulated muscle GLUT4 to reverse insulin resistance.

Skeletal muscle biopsies and functional assessments confirmed that GlyNAC reduced muscle p16INK4a senescence, γH2AX DNA damage, and plasma 8-OHdG while restoring walking speed, 6-minute walk distance, and grip strength.

companionLifespanNote: Companion Mammalian Lifespan Proof (Kumar et al., Nutrients 2022, PMID: 35334909): In a parallel study in C57BL/6J mice starting at 65 weeks of age (~50 human years), dietary GlyNAC supplementation extended median lifespan by +24.2% in both males and females (from 104.0 to 129.0 weeks, p < 0.0001) while restoring cardiac, hepatic, and renal GSH synthesis and mitophagy.

keyFindings.title: Why GlyNAC Works Where Direct GSH or NAC Alone Fails
keyFindings.desc: Oral glutathione is degraded in the gut, and cells tightly regulate internal GSH to prevent reductive stress. Providing both limiting precursors (glycine + cysteine as NAC) allows tissues to synthesize exact physiological amounts of GSH on demand.

keyFindings.title: Young Adults Showed No Over-Correction ('No Reductive Stress')
keyFindings.desc: Giving GlyNAC to young adults (aged 21–40) for 2 weeks did not push their already-normal GSH above baseline or induce reductive stress—confirming autoregulated cellular synthesis.

keyFindings.title: Simultaneous Reversal of 9 Aging Defects in Muscle & Blood
keyFindings.desc: In skeletal muscle biopsies and plasma, 16 weeks of GlyNAC improved GSH deficiency, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, mitophagy, inflammation, insulin resistance, endothelial dysfunction, genomic damage (γH2AX/8-OHdG), and p16INK4a senescence.

keyFindings.title: Washout Confirmations & +24.2% Mouse Lifespan Extension
keyFindings.desc: In the prior 24-week pilot trial (PMID: 33783984), stopping GlyNAC for 12 weeks caused GSH and physical benefits to recede toward baseline, proving causal dependence; in mice (PMID: 35334909), lifelong late-onset GlyNAC extended lifespan by +24.2%.

conclusions.title: The 'Power of 3': Glycine + Cysteine (NAC) + Glutathione
conclusions.content: Beyond serving as GSH substrates, glycine provides one-carbon methyl-group and NMDA/collagen support while NAC supplies sulfane sulfur and redox signaling—creating a three-way synergy.

conclusions.title: Age-Stratified Indication: Greatest Benefit After Age 55–60
conclusions.content: Because intracellular RBC glutathione remains preserved in healthy 20–40-year-olds and declines steeply after age 55–60, GlyNAC is specifically indicated for middle-aged and older adults or states of elevated oxidative/metabolic stress.

conclusions.title: Rapid 2-to-16-Week Biomarker Responsiveness
conclusions.content: Significant improvements in RBC GSH (+121%), TBARS (-42%), and HOMA-IR (-31%) were already detectable at Week 2, reaching young-adult equivalence by Week 16.

protocolImplications: Translational takeaway: The Baylor RCT used weight-adjusted dosing of 100 mg/kg/day Glycine + 100 mg/kg/day N-Acetylcysteine (roughly 7 g/day of each for a 70 kg adult, split into morning and evening doses), while real-world clinical protocols commonly titrate from 1.8–3.6 g/day up to 6–7 g/day in adults aged 55+ or those with verified low RBC glutathione, elevated hs-CRP, or elevated HOMA-IR. Because young adults with normal GSH showed no change, testing baseline RBC Glutathione, GGT, hs-CRP, and HOMA-IR helps identify responders.
